newsitem.title: USA: U.S. military prepares possible Zaire evacuation.
newsitem.headline: U.S. military prepares possible Zaire evacuation.

text.p: The U.S. military is making contingency preparations for the possible removal of Americans from Zaire but has received no request to do so from the U.S. embassy there, the Pentagon said on Thursday.

"We have sent in an assessment team and we are taking prudent efforts beyond that to be ready to do whatever we are requested to do," Defense Department spokesman Ken Bacon told reporters. But he said he did not believe U.S. military aircraft or helicopters had been moved to the region for a possible evacuation.

Bacon told reporters in response to questions that a 30-member U.S. military team sent to Zaire on Wednesday was still assessing an anti-government rebellion there and the possible use of roads, airfields and communications in the emergency movement of Americans.

He said Zaire remained unsettled and the United States was aware of reports a possible coup attempt might be made against ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko, who is reportedly preparing to return to the capital of Kinshasa on Friday.

"The talk is in the wind and I think we have to pay attention to the fact that there could be rapid change in Kinshasa," Bacon said. But he stressed that no request had been made by the embassy there to remove Americans.

There are believed to be about 650 Americans in the central African nation, including those working for the American government. France has advised its citizens to leave Zaire and has moved aircraft and about 100 troops to neighbouring Gabon and Congo to be ready for any evacuation of French citizens.
